summary: Active Pass Light on Georgina Point, Mayne Island, was first lit on 10 June 1885; its keeper Henry Georgeson tended it for 35 years, through fog, currents and a 1918 grounding.

access.note: Visible from the Tsawwassen-Swartz Bay ferry; reached by road from the Mayne Island ferry terminal to Georgina Point Road. The tower is a working light; no source says it is open to the public inside.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (navigation aid); Gulf Islands National Park Reserve (property since 2006)

events.note: Henry Georgeson appointed keeper by order in council, 21 July 1884
Square wooden tower, 12.8 m (42 ft) to the vane of the lantern, with keeper's dwelling attached (as quoted by the biography from the deputy minister's June 1885 report)
Steam fog alarm replaces the bell
Santa Barbara struck in Active Pass; listed among vessels given assistance in the year ended 31 March 1908; no date or detail given
Fixed white light changed to occulting white (petroleum vapour); biography gives 1910; the Department's report for the year ended 31 March 1911 records the change
Princess Adelaide grounded in dense fog in front of the light, 13 October 1918, the foghorn working; no loss of life; refloated
Original 1885 tower replaced by a square dwelling surmounted by a lantern room
Cylindrical concrete tower with lantern and galley built to serve as the light; square dwelling kept for the keeper
Last keeper, Jean Beaudet, left; station de-staffed
Property transferred to Gulf Islands National Park Reserve; Canadian Coast Guard keeps the navigation aids

keepers.name: Henry Georgeson
keepers.note: Known as Scotty. Appointed by order in council 21 July 1884; lit the light 10 June 1885; retired 31 December 1920. Lighthouse Friends gives 1885 to 1920. The Department's 1906 keeper table lists him at the Active Pass Light and Fog Whistle.

keepers.name: George Georgeson
keepers.note: Son of Henry Georgeson. The biography says Henry paid him as assistant out of the salary raised for the fog alarm; the year given is when that salary rose, not a documented start date.

keepers.name: Clarence Edgar Carver
keepers.note: Lighthouse Friends only. Its term overlaps Gurney's to 1945.

keepers.name: Jean Beaudet
keepers.note: Last keeper; Lighthouse Friends gives his departure in 1997.

wrecks.outcome: Struck in Active Pass; listed among vessels given assistance in the year ended 31 March 1908; the entry gives no date, cause or detail

Grounded in dense fog on the rocks in front of the light, the foghorn working; no loss of life; refloated. Inquiry at Victoria in November 1918 found the master and second officer in default; master's certificate suspended two months, second officer's six months.

evidence.supports: Third lighthouse on the site; 1950s and 1960s modernization
evidence.quote: The third lighthouse built on the site, the Active Pass Lighthouse reflects the modernization and evolution of marine aids to navigation in the 1950s and 1960s.

evidence.supports: Since 1885 the station has served marine traffic
evidence.quote: Since its establishment in 1885, the Active Pass lightstation has made it easier and safer for marine traffic to travel between Victoria and Vancouver.

evidence.supports: Concrete tower, apple core plan, minimal maintenance
evidence.quote: Built with common and durable materials from a variation of a standard “apple core” plan, the lighthouse is a clear expression of functional design and the Department of Transport’s desire to minimize maintenance.

evidence.supports: Symbol of the Mayne Island community
evidence.quote: The lighthouse is a symbol of the Mayne Island community.

evidence.supports: Receives numerous visitors

corrections.proposed: 1885 tower was wood (replaced 1940 by a square dwelling with lantern room); concrete tower built 1969
corrections.why: The 1885 light was a wooden tower as the biography quotes the 1885 report; Lighthouse Friends dates the concrete tower to 1969. The 13.7 m height is not checked in these sources.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record says sources differ on whether the light is still lit. The Coast Guard's List of Lights (entry 275) gives the light as an operating aid, Fl W 10s, year round.
The record lists different first years. The first light was 1885 (biography and Lighthouse Friends). Later towers are 1940 and 1969.

notes_for_editor: (1) The keepers after Georgeson (Gurney 1921-1945, Carver, Ruck, DeRousie, Beaudet) come only from Lighthouse Friends. The keeper tables for 1921-1924 in the local corpus did not show the station under a search for its name, so those names are unverified. (2) The record's events list has 1969 first_lit and 1969 deactivated. The sources give 1969 as the year a new concrete tower was built to serve as the light; nothing found says the light was put out in 1969. Please check whether the 1969 first_lit and deactivated events should be changed. (3) The name Princess Adelaide is matched to the 13 October 1918 remark in the Department's wreck table by position in the OCR, since the vessel names are printed in a separate column. The biography names the Princess Adelaide for the same date and place. The officers' names (R. A. Hunter, H. A. Ormiston) are in the finding text of the same entry. Checked 2026-10-27: the names column and the remarks column run in the same order, and the entry after the 13 October one is the Princess Sophia, stranded and lost on 25 October 1918 on Vanderbilt reef, Lynn Canal, so the match holds. The page image was not viewed. The story prints no officer names. (4) The occulting-light change: the biography says 1910; the report for the year ended 31 March 1911 records it as done. The story gives both. (5) The 1885 description is quoted through the Dictionary of Canadian Biography, which quotes the deputy minister's June 1885 report; the original sessional paper was not in the local corpus. (6) Santa Barbara: the report gives no date beyond the year ended 31 March 1908, no cause, and no location beyond the pass. The story says so. (7) Accounts of the 1918 fog differ: the biography says dense fog; the inquiry finding says heavy weather. Both are in the story. (8) Lighthouse Friends calls the Sand Heads post an assistant keeper's job; the biography says only 'a position on the Sand Heads lightship', so the story uses the biography's words. (9) The biography's permalink is 15E; the page read was the 15F address, which carries the same text. (10) No photos sourced.
